messages:
natalie_sales: Quick thread - VertexCorp asked whether we can provide a short list of stable egress IPs for a 10-day PrivateLink POC. Their security team only accepts IP allowlists (no domain rules) and they perform TLS interception. Looping @omar_neteng and @gina_platform.

omar_neteng: Short answer: yes, for Dedicated we can route egress through our NAT appliance and allocate 2-3 Elastic IPs per region. That avoids touching their proxy certs. If they insist on using their proxy with TLS MITM, they'll need to trust our client certs or we can attempt basic auth header support (no NTLM/Kerberos).

gina_platform: Pricing ballpark for a 10-day POC: one-time setup $1,000; prorated Dedicated compute ~$1,200; EIP/NAT appliance prorated ~$200; estimated egress charge (sample 100GB) ~$20. We can offer a flat POC bundle $2,200 to keep procurement simple. Hosted would be ~35% cheaper but can't guarantee static egress.

omar_neteng: Example firewall snippet (customer outbound allowlist) - we'll swap final EIPs before kickoff:
```
# VertexCorp firewall / proxy allowlist (egress to Redwood)
ALLOW TCP 443 TO 18.205.32.10,18.205.32.11  # control-plane EIPs (us-west-2)
ALLOW TCP 8443 TO 18.205.32.20               # runtime plane EIP (dedicated)
DNS: allow outbound to their resolver or 9.9.9.9
```
Note: if their proxy blocks gRPC on 8443 we can tunnel over 443 with HTTP/1.1 as fallback.

infra-bot: Calendar: POC kickoff tentative 2098848000 (invite sent). Owners: natalie_sales (owner), gina_platform (tech lead), omar_neteng (network).

natalie_sales: Action items: 1) omar -> publish final EIP list and polished firewall doc (ETA 24h). 2) gina -> finalize POC quote + simple SOW (ETA 24h). 3) natalie -> upload VertexCorp sec-questions and ask for expected token/day. Will update once they pick NAT EIPs vs proxy-auth. :thumbsup:
